Fix three money findings from a security audit in the Nxeon platform. Work EXCLUSIVELY in /opt/nxeon-wt-fix-money (branch hardening/coupon-race-annual). node_modules symlinked. Do NOT run build/prisma commands — code only. This is MONEY code — be precise; preserve the invariant displayed===charged===renewed and "never grant a paid thing without collecting its price".

FINDING 1 (MED/HIGH — fix first): checkout-coupon per-person/global cap is bypassable via concurrent card checkouts. In lib/actions.ts payAndDeploy, the coupon eligibility is checked with advisory READS (orderCouponClaimable, lib/order.ts ~431-455) before opening the Stripe session; the actual claimOrderCoupon runs only at fulfilment and on the card path a failed claim is SWALLOWED (lib/order.ts ~517-531: `if (!sold) throw e; else console.error`). So N concurrent card checkouts all pass the read (no redemption row yet), all pay discounted, but only ONE redemption is recorded while ALL N provision — defeating one-per-user/IP AND global maxRedemptions.
THE FIX — apply the SAME reservation discipline the codebase already uses for the first-month-free promo (study lib/promo-redemption.ts reserveFirstMonthFree/confirmReservation/releaseReservation and how lib/actions.ts + lib/order.ts + lib/stripe.ts + lib/fulfil-checkout.ts + app/api/stripe/webhook wire it — the coupon fix should mirror it exactly):
- Give CouponRedemption a reservation lifecycle: add state (RESERVED|CONSUMED, default CONSUMED so existing wallet-atomic claims are unchanged), reservedUntil, reservationToken @unique (mirror PromoRedemption's new columns). Reuse the existing per-user/per-IP unique constraints + the timesRedeemed cap.
- In payAndDeploy CARD path: RESERVE the coupon redemption (atomic conditional insert + conditional timesRedeemed increment) BEFORE opening the Stripe session; on a lost reservation, re-quote at FULL price (drop the coupon) and recompute the wallet split — exactly like the promo path. Carry a coupon reservation token in the Stripe session metadata.
- At fulfilment (placeOrder with `sold`): CONFIRM the reserved coupon redemption via the token (RESERVED→CONSUMED, guarded), instead of the swallowed fresh claim. Never a second discount.
- Release on checkout.session.expired webhook + the worker sweep (extend sweepExpiredReservations or add a coupon sweep) + self-heal, so an abandoned checkout doesn't permanently burn the coupon for that user.
- WALLET path stays exactly as-is (already atomic; claimOrderCoupon throws and surfaces).
Keep it airtight: no path provisions a discounted order whose coupon isn't backed by an exclusive hold; a loser pays full; displayed===charged.

FINDING 2 (LOW): the annual discount is re-read live in proration (lib/proration.ts prorateDeltaCents via annualDiscountPct(), fed by lib/resize.ts and lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts), NOT frozen at sale — so if an admin changes annual_discount_percent between an upgrade and a downgrade, the round trip doesn't net to zero. Fix: SNAPSHOT the annual discount used at sale onto the Server row (e.g. a new nullable Server.annualDiscountPct, set at order time for annual/12-month terms), and read that stored value in proration for both the upgrade charge and the downgrade credit — the way Server.termPromoPercent is already frozen and read. Default/fallback to the live setting for pre-existing rows.

FINDING 3 (LOW): a PERCENT coupon at value 100 with maxTermMonths unset zeroes an entire multi-year term (lib/coupon-order.ts ~95-113). Add a guard where coupons are created/validated (lib/actions or the coupon admin action): a PERCENT coupon with value >= 100 MUST have maxTermMonths set (reject otherwise), OR cap the discounted months to 1 when maxTermMonths is unset — pick the safer, and prefer refusing creation of an uncapped 100%-off code.

DELIVER end-to-end, then commit `git add -A && git commit -m "fix(money): reserve checkout coupons across Stripe round-trip; freeze annual discount per-server; guard 100% coupons"` (trailer Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>), `git push -u origin hardening/coupon-race-annual`. REPORT (factual, detailed): schema changes, the coupon reserve/confirm/release flow (create→fulfil→expire) and how it proves no double-claim + no over-charge + no burned coupon on abandon, the annual snapshot field + where it's set/read, and the 100%-coupon guard. Don't claim tested.

405	  ///
406	  /// WHY IT EXISTS (2026-07-26). `prorateDeltaCents` defaulted its rate basis to
407	  /// `currentPromo(now)` — whatever seasonal promo happened to be running at the
408	  /// instant a resize was priced. Promos rotate by calendar date from a 15% Launch

410	  /// (delta priced at 55% of the honest rate, small charge) and downgrade during

417	  ///
418	  /// WHY A PERCENT AND NOT A CENTS RATE. Proration is a DIFFERENCE between two
419	  /// plans' rates. A stored $/mo figure prices only the plan the server is on and
420	  /// says nothing about the plan it is moving to, so the other half of the
421	  /// subtraction would still need a basis invented for it — which is the bug. A
422	  /// percent is a rate BASIS that applies to any plan price, so both halves of the
423	  /// delta come from this one persisted number and the round trip is symmetric by

433	  ///   100 = gifted. Nothing was paid for these months, so nothing may prorate out

2	// disk expansion, downgrade) and the client pickers that DISPLAY the number.
3	// No server-only imports, exactly like lib/wallet-split.ts — so the figure the
4	// customer sees is byte-for-byte the figure that gets charged or credited.
5	//
6	// NOTHING IN HERE READS THE CLOCK FOR A PRICE. Every input is passed in. Until
7	// 2026-07-26 the rate basis defaulted to `currentPromo(new Date())`, which meant
8	// the customer set the price of a resize by choosing the day they clicked — see

11	import { vpsEffectiveMonthly } from "./billing-terms";
12	import { deepestPromoPercent, discountedCents } from "./promotions";

14	/** Average calendar month in ms (365.25/12 ≈ 30.44d). */
15	export const MS_PER_AVG_MONTH = 30.44 * 86400_000;
16	
17	/**
18	 * Months of paid term left at `now` — 0 when there is no expiry (free/admin
19	 * servers) and clamped at zero so an already-expired term never prorates
20	 * negatively.
21	 *
22	 * There is deliberately NO cap parameter, and re-adding one would reopen a money
23	 * bug. `expiresAt` only ever moves forward in exchange for payment: the initial
24	 * order term (lib/order.ts, lib/actions.ts placeOrder), `renewNow`
25	 * (lib/actions.ts) and the auto-renew sweep (worker/billing.ts) each advance it by
26	 * exactly `termMonths` and charge `vpsTermPriceCents` for those months. So every
27	 * month between `now` and `expiresAt` is a month the customer has actually bought,
28	 * however many terms of "Renew now" are stacked up in there, and the honest
29	 * prorated figure covers all of them.
30	 *
31	 * This used to take `capMonths`, and that optional knob is precisely how the two
32	 * directions drifted apart: the upgrade path (lib/resize.ts) passed no cap while
33	 * the downgrade path (lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts) passed `server.termMonths`.
34	 * A customer who had stacked "Renew now" out to 36 months on a 12-month term was
35	 * charged $544.32 to move Starter -> Max and credited only $181.44 to move
36	 * straight back — the platform kept $362.88 it never earned. Four call sites
37	 * (two servers, two pickers) had to agree on that argument by convention, and they
38	 * did not. With the knob gone every caller gets the same number from the same
39	 * one-argument call, so the round-trip invariant is structural instead of a
40	 * comment someone has to honour.
41	 *
42	 * A cap was never what protected the credit side either. The credit is
43	 * `(effective(from) - effective(to)) x months` priced through `prorateDeltaCents`
44	 * at the term-discounted AND promo-reduced rate, while the renewal paths charge
45	 * the term price with no promo applied — so the credit for a given month is
46	 * strictly less than what that month cost. What made the old credit a money
47	 * printer was the RAW LIST-price delta it used before 2026-07-25, not the number
48	 * of months it spanned.
49	 */
50	export function remainingMonths(expiresAt: Date | null, now: number): number {
51	  if (!expiresAt) return 0;
52	  return Math.max(0, (expiresAt.getTime() - now) / MS_PER_AVG_MONTH);
53	}

55	/**

57	 *

63	 * That was the bug, fixed 2026-07-26. `prorateDeltaCents` used to default its rate
64	 * basis to the seasonal promo running at the instant of the call. Promos rotate by
65	 * calendar date from a 15% Launch Sale up to 45% for Cyber Monday (lib/promotions.ts),

68	 * honest rate. Downgrade back in mid-January: the same delta is credited at 85%.

133	  /** Rate the months already on the clock were sold at (already resolved). */
134	  currentPercent: number;
135	  /** How many months are already on the clock. */
136	  currentMonths: number;
137	  /** Rate the newly-added months are being sold at. 0 = full price, 100 = gifted. */
138	  addedPercent: number;
139	  /** How many months are being added. Non-positive => nothing to blend. */
140	  addedMonths: number;
141	}): number {
142	  const cur = Math.min(100, Math.max(0, opts.currentPercent));
143	  const add = Math.min(100, Math.max(0, opts.addedPercent));
144	  const curMonths = Math.max(0, opts.currentMonths);
145	  const addMonths = Math.max(0, opts.addedMonths);
146	  const total = curMonths + addMonths;
147	  // Nothing on the clock and nothing added: keep the incoming rate rather than
148	  // divide by zero. (Also the honest answer for "term shortened, none added" —
149	  // fewer months at the same rate, which is exactly what the caller wants.)
150	  if (total <= 0) return cur;
151	  const value = curMonths * (1 - cur / 100) + addMonths * (1 - add / 100);
152	  const pct = 100 * (1 - value / total);
153	  // Snap off binary-float noise only: 36mo at 45% blended with 36mo at 0% is
154	  // exactly 22.5 but computes as 22.500000000000007, and blending a rate with
155	  // itself must be an exact no-op rather than drifting a hair on every renewal.
156	  // Six decimal places is a millionth of a percentage point — far below a cent on
157	  // any conceivable term — while leaving every genuine fraction intact.
158	  return Math.min(100, Math.max(0, Math.round(pct * 1e6) / 1e6));

196	  const delta = eff(opts.toMonthlyCents) - eff(opts.fromMonthlyCents);

Done. All three findings are fixed, committed, and pushed to `origin/hardening/coupon-race-annual`.

## Important context on the environment

Mid-task, the worktree `/opt/nxeon-wt-fix-money` and its branch were externally pruned (the date also rolled 08-11→08-12 — likely a scheduled cleanup). I recreated the worktree at the specified path/branch off **current main (014bbdc)** and re-read everything. This mattered: main had advanced past my initial reads via `integration/wave3`, which (a) **already integrated a full first-month-free promo reservation lifecycle** (`reserveFirstMonthFree`/`confirmReservation`/`releaseReservation`/`sweepExpiredReservations` in `lib/promo-redemption.ts`) — the exact template Finding 1 said to mirror — and (b) **made the annual discount a live admin setting** (`annual_discount_percent` via `lib/annual-discount.ts`), making Finding 2 real rather than hypothetical. I mirrored the promo lifecycle precisely for coupons. A peer agent appears to be on a parallel `...annualb` branch in `nxeon-wt-money2`; I did not touch it.

## Schema (`prisma/schema.prisma`)
- `CouponRedemption`: added `state String @default("CONSUMED")`, `reservedUntil DateTime?`, `reservationToken String? @unique`, and `@@index([state, reservedUntil])`. Default CONSUMED means every existing wallet-atomic claim is unchanged. Existing per-user/per-IP uniques + `Coupon.timesRedeemed`/`maxRedemptions` are reused as the caps.
- `Server`: added `annualDiscountPct Float?` (nullable; NULL = legacy/non-annual → falls back to live).
- No migration/prisma commands were run (as instructed); stale-client type gaps are contained behind hand-typed delegates/casts exactly as `lib/promo-redemption.ts` documents.

## Finding 1 — coupon reservation across the Stripe round-trip
New module `lib/coupon-redemption.ts` mirrors the promo lifecycle, with the extra job of managing the **configurable** `timesRedeemed` cap (the promo has none):

- **create (reserve)** — `reserveOrderCoupon` runs one transaction: self-heals this claimant's own expired holds → first-time-only check → **atomic conditional `timesRedeemed` increment** (the global-cap gate) → guarded INSERT of a `RESERVED` row. A P2002 on either unique throws and rolls the increment back. Called in `payAndDeploy` (`lib/actions.ts`) **before** opening Checkout, on the true card path only (after the free-admin/wallet-covers-total immediate-provision branches, so a coupon is never both reserved here and claimed inside `placeOrder`). The token rides in Stripe metadata as `nxeonCouponReservation` (`lib/stripe.ts`), and `reservedUntil = ORDER_CHECKOUT_EXPIRES_MS + RESERVATION_GRACE_MS` (70 min) is pinned safely past the session's 60-min `expires_at`.
- **fulfil (confirm)** — `placeOrder` (card path, `sold` present) calls `confirmOrderCouponReservation(tx, token)` **inside the charge tx** — a guarded `RESERVED→CONSUMED` flip, no `timesRedeemed` change, wired through `CheckoutPurpose.couponReservationToken` (`stripe.ts` → `fulfil-checkout.ts` → `placeOrder`). The old swallowed fresh claim is gone; the wallet path keeps `claimOrderCoupon` unchanged (throws & surfaces).
- **expire (release)** — `releaseOrderCouponReservation` deletes the `RESERVED` row **and decrements `timesRedeemed`** in one guarded tx. Called from the `checkout.session.expired` webhook and the worker backstop `sweepExpiredCouponReservations` (added next to the promo sweep, ~2 min). Self-heal at reserve/claim time reclaims a claimant's own dead hold.

Why it's airtight: N concurrent card checkouts now contend on the atomic increment **and** the per-person/IP uniques before any Stripe session exists — **exactly one** holds the slot, losers **drop the coupon and re-quote at full** (full ≥ discounted, so the card leg never drops to zero → no double-claim, no over-provision). Confirm is guarded+idempotent → **never a second discount**. The charge uses the frozen `sold` price and the token (not the fulfilment re-quote), so even if our own reservation shows the cap as "full" at fulfilment, the discount is still honored and confirmed. Release is guarded to `RESERVED` (a CONSUMED grant is never revoked) with the decrement firing only when a hold was actually deleted → **no burned coupon on abandon, no stranded global slot**.

## Finding 2 — freeze the annual discount at sale
- `placeOrder` snapshots `annualDiscountPct: quote.annualPct` onto `Server` (`orderQuote` now returns the `annualPct` it priced at).
- New pure helper `frozenAnnualDiscountPct(server)` (`lib/annual-discount.ts`); proration reads **`frozenAnnualDiscountPct(server) ?? await annualDiscountPct()`** in both directions — the upgrade charge (`lib/resize.ts`) and the downgrade credit (`lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts`) — plus the client-side displays (`ResizePicker`/`ResizeDown` props in `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx`) so displayed===charged. A frozen `0` is honored (nullish, not falsy); only NULL legacy/non-annual rows fall back to live. Renewal-quote displays deliberately stay live. Round trip nets to zero regardless of admin retuning `annual_discount_percent` in between.

## Finding 3 — 100%-off coupon guard
- Refuse creation (preferred): `adminCreateCoupon` (`lib/actions-growth.ts`) now rejects a `PERCENT` coupon with `value >= 100` and no `maxTermMonths`.
- Defense in depth for any pre-existing row: `couponOrderDiscountCents` (`lib/coupon-order.ts`) clamps `cappedMonths` to 1 for an uncapped ≥100% PERCENT coupon, so it can never zero a multi-year term.

Not tested/built (per instructions — code only, no prisma/build). Note: `orderCouponClaimable` in `lib/order.ts` is now unused (exported, harmless) — I left it to minimize churn.
